stem: Why do nurse staffing committees include direct-care nurse representation?

options.A: To incorporate frontline knowledge of patient acuity, care needs, workload, and staff skills into unit staffing plans.
options.B: To exclude direct-care nurses from staffing decisions so planning remains entirely administrative.
options.C: To use one fixed staffing number for every shift without considering acuity, workload, or skill mix.
options.D: To transfer staffing decisions to personnel with no direct knowledge of unit-level patient-care demands.

rationale: ANA describes staffing committees as nurse-led groups that develop unit-level staffing plans based on patient population acuity and needs together with staff skills and experience, and supports substantial direct-care nurse representation. Direct-care nurses contribute frontline knowledge of actual patient-care demands and staffing conditions. A is correct.
educational_objective: Explain why direct-care nurses belong on staffing committees: their frontline knowledge helps align staffing plans with patient acuity, care needs, workload, and staff skills.

audit_findings.source_authority: ANA safe-staffing advocacy guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: ANA staffing-committee and direct-care representation discussion
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately ties representation to frontline input on patient-care demand and staffing-plan design without asserting a fixed staffing ratio.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because it is the opposite of direct-care representation.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because safe staffing considers acuity, workload, needs and skill mix rather than one fixed number.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the purpose of representation is to include—not remove—unit-level clinical knowledge.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A explains the intended function of direct-care representation.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives address the rationale for staffing-committee membership.
